I think the best way to do it, is simply by making a nice, quick break, that is from a place of kindness in your heart, not ultimatum or anger or assumption. 

A woman sets the moral tone of a relationship. You are simply resetting the tone, regardless of what or what does not continue, you are setting your bar to a certain height, at this time. 

I would say to him,

“I want you to know that I have really found most of my comfort lately by turning my heart fully to Allah. I enjoyed our time together, but moving forward, I’m living my best, modest life, so we won’t be able to see each other anymore and no hard feelings or drama, I’ve got to go now, bye.”

End it. Nicely. It doesn’t give him an ultimatum. It allows him time to process what you’ve said, and who knows, maybe you will inspire him to turn his heart to Allah as well, without suggesting it, without trying to force him into it, and without punishing him or giving him a bad attitude, and without you holding any victim cards. 

This style of break up is comprehensive, modern and relatable, because you are taking responsibility for your religion, lifestyle & relationship. 😊

And be a bit cheerful when you say it. Worshipping Allah isn’t a sad experience. 🌺

I think people think Mass is just Greater Boston. In reality most of Mass is NOT Greater Boston.

items.title: "Unless all of us - Muslims, Christians, Jews, people of faith, people of no faith - come together to stop this madness, all of us will collectively suffer." - Sh. Yasir Qadhi
items.text: "Unless all of us - Muslims, Christians, Jews, people of faith, people of no faith - come together to stop this madness, all of us will collectively suffer." - Sh. Yasir Qadhi

It’s not easy.

My sister and I do not wear our hijabs often. We live in the North, in the US, in an intolerant area. 

When we go to the mosque on Fridays, we have pepper spray in our socks. We have discussed a plan for if shooters enter the building, AND the entire time we are praying, we are all watching not only our Imam, but also,  7 cameras positioned around our building and cars. 

My sister was dragged by police, from our minivan, mere blocks from our Masjid. She was accused of a crime she didn’t commit, right in the middle of the street, held for a while there, then let go. 

This is the very first year we put up just a couple of lanterns in the window and a streamer for Ramadan.
And there are beautiful Muslims who want friends like us as well, so the more we get out, as Muslims, the more chances we have to meet each other.🌸🌸🌸

Sometimes when things are darkest, is when everything turns around. Try some charity. Go out. Do something for someone else.

When I felt like that, I went for three days in a row to clean an old ladies yard. 

The manual labor took my mind off things, and the entire experience put me in a better mood. 

Let me know how you feel.
